record.paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: For a fixed codimension r, determine the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and type t is unimodal.

evidence.quote: For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest type t for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $R = k[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ the polynomial ring in $r$ variables. A monomial order ideal $X$ is a finite set of monomials of $R$ that is closed under taking divisors (if $m \in X$ and $m'$ divides $m$, then $m' \in X$). The order ideal $X$ is called pure of type $t$ if all of its maximal monomials (with respect to divisibility) have the same degree and there are exactly $t$ of them. The pure O-sequence associated with $X$ is the vector $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_e)$ where $h_i$ is the number of monomials of degree $i$ in $X$; in particular $h_0 = 1$, $h_1 \le r$, and $h_e = t$. A finite sequence of nonnegative integers is called unimodal if it does not strictly increase after a strict decrease, i.e., there exists an index $j$ such that $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_e$.

For each fixed integer $r \ge 1$, determine the largest integer $t = t(r)$ (if such a largest integer exists) such that every pure O-sequence of codimension $r$ (meaning $h_1 = r$) and type $t$ is unimodal.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of determining the codimension-versus-type unimodality threshold $t(r)$ is open. Partial results exist: pure O-sequences in codimension at most 2 are always unimodal; in codimension 3, type 2 is unimodal (Boij–Migliore–Miró-Roig–Nagel–Zanello), and Boyle (2014) proved the type-3, codimension-3 case is also unimodal; for codimension 3 and large type, non-unimodal examples are known (in fact, for any $r\ge 3$ and $M\ge 1$ there exist pure O-sequences in $r$ variables with $M$ maxima). The exact threshold for any $r\ge 3$ has not been determined.

status_evidence.title: The unimodality of pure O-sequences of type three in three variables
status_evidence.snippet: Artinian level monomial algebras of type three in three variables have unimodal Hilbert functions.
status_evidence.claim: Type 3 in codimension 3 is unimodal (Boyle, 2014), extending earlier results for type 2.

status_evidence.title: On the shape of a pure O-sequence
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph studying the shape and unimodality of pure O-sequences, including non-unimodal examples in codimension 3 with many maxima.
status_evidence.claim: Non-unimodal pure O-sequences with arbitrarily many peaks exist in codimension r ≥ 3, so the threshold t(r) is finite for r ≥ 3 but its exact value is unknown.
